newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel little changed vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel little changed vs dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel changed little against the dollar on Thursday in mixed and aimless trading, dealers said.

"Trading was mixed today with no clear trend. The shekel rose slightly because the business sector was converting dollars into shekels for mid-month tax payments," said Ilan Zadka at United Mizrahi Bank.
Zadka said investors had to convert money on Thursday because workers, dramatising their demand for a five-day work week, plan to shut down Israel's banks on Friday.
"The Bank of Israel had to intervene again in the market after the basket fell by more than seven percent below the diagonal rate," Zadka said.
Traders estimated that the central bank bought less than $90 million.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3410 shekels against 3.3420 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6349 shekels against 3.6337 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6938 shekels per 100 yen against 2.6940 on Wednesday and against the mark at 1.9866 shekels against 1.9819 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3400 shekels.
